answers.ask: No setting was given - should the maps be modern military, sci-fi, or bright and cartoonish?
answers.answer: Use a bright, cartoonish shooter style so the weapons, skins, and wraps feel fun and readable.

answers.ask: Which space should be built first: the lobby, the practice range, or a match map?
answers.answer: Build the lobby first, since it is the hub for matchmaking, weapon unlocks, skin boxes, wrap boxes, and entering the practice arena.

answers.ask: Which game modes do you want - team deathmatch, free-for-all, objective modes?
answers.answer: Include team deathmatch and free-for-all first; keep objective modes out of the initial build.

scene_prompt: Create a bright, cartoonish 3D shooter lobby as the central hub. Arrange a welcoming open lobby space with distinct areas for matchmaking, weapon unlock displays, skin boxes, and wrap boxes, plus a clearly marked entrance leading into a separate practice arena. Include the practice arena as an adjacent combat space, and provide connections from the lobby to match maps for team deathmatch and free-for-all.
agent_notes: Self-declared 3D shooter, so Shooter leads, but the author answered the shape question directly: build the lobby first, because it is the hub for matchmaking, unlocks, skin and wrap boxes, and entry to the practice arena. That makes hub-portals the shape from the shared catalogue rather than any of Shooter's match-map shapes — the space being built exists to send players onward — and its P4 is earned, since the match maps and the practice arena are genuinely separate from the lobby rather than one continuous world. Aim Trainer is the only preset whose options survive that: station-loadout becomes the lobby's weapon racks and box-opening stations, and target-practice covers the practice arena downrange of a firing line; every competitive-mode preset would have imported team bases and lanes into a lobby. With no user to ask, I treated the 15 weapons, the skins and the wraps as inventory content with no geometry of their own beyond those stations, and left the team deathmatch and free-for-all maps out of this build since the author asked for the lobby first and deferred objective modes.
